sources.says: AAJ 1997 summary: IV+ 5.9 95° couloir climbed in steps with 'a little ice protection'; no pitch-by-pitch text retrievable. Entry's own notes: about two pitches, protection available.
Route is a steep gully with hardest ground in a few pitches; no WI5 rating found independently. The entry text itself calls this a near-vertical ice pitch with a belay at its base.
First-ascent account: 'two pitches through unconsolidated snow over moderate rock' after the steep snow, then a rock band.
Route listed as steep snow/mixed with no continuous glacier travel; gear includes rock pro.
After the M6 notch crack, party traverses into the final couloir of the North Buttress Couloir route; the entry's own notes call it one more steep mixed pitch. Grade not stated by source.
(search snippet only, page 403) NE Face is a technical snow/ice/rock route (Beckey-Rupley 1971) climbing an 'objective ice apron' across crevasses; entry notes say screws needed. Route ice_grade AI3.
2019 trip report: leftward traverse then climbed 2 long pitches after the lower bergschrund (party simul-climbed them).
Account of the line: 30-40° snow to first schrund, 50 ft serac crux (70-85°), more steep snow/ice above.

Standard Fremont Glacier route is roped glacier travel, no belayed ice; AI1 is a rating of walking-angle glacier, not a pitch. Based on route description in the entry plus general knowledge; no source page retrieved.
Moderate-incline glacier to the Hogsback; moat crossing is a step, not a pitch. No source page retrieved.
Mountain Project describes a 'short ice pitch (70-80 degrees)' above Thumb Rock with an option to traverse around; entry notes a water-ice pitch through the Gun Sight when formed.
'Climb several pitches of 40-60 degree ice and negotiate steep glacier travel until gaining the Liberty Cap Glacier.'
'Climb a few short (5-8 ft) vertical ice sections to surpass the bergschrund'; photo caption 'crossing the bergschrund before the final ice pitches to Liberty Cap'.

sources.says: Right variation: ice/rock to the exit chute, a short vertical rock step with one or two pins; protection 'may include ice screws, a pin rack and/or light rock rack'; 45-55° ice near the buttress.
Willis Wall is a Grade V face whose upper ice steps beneath the ice cliff are climbed belayed; route ice_grade AI3. No source page confirmed pitch style.
(search snippet) SW Couloir and Face is WI3/5.2, Grade III; entry notes name the vertical ice in a corner as steepest ice, 18 m, needs screws and a second tool.
(search snippet) Route graded WI3; 'steepest sustained ground' per entry notes, protected by screws and pickets.
